name: Global X Uranium ETF
note: ETF — included because URA is a central subject of this uranium-sector bookmark.
blurb: The Global X Uranium ETF (URA) tracks the Solactive Global Uranium & Nuclear Components Total Return Index, a broad-market-capitalisation-weighted benchmark spanning roughly fifty companies across the nuclear fuel cycle: uranium mining, milling, refining, enrichment, and reactor-equipment manufacturing. Launched in 2010, URA is the largest and most liquid pure-uranium-exposure ETF by assets, with approximately $5 billion in AUM as of 2025. Its expense ratio is 0.69%. The fund's largest holding is Cameco Corporation at roughly 23% of assets, followed by Oklo Inc. Class A (a small modular reactor developer) at ~11% — an unusual position for a 'miner' ETF that reflects URA's willingness to include the broader nuclear technology value chain. Other top holdings include Uranium Energy Corp., NexGen Energy, and Centrus Energy. URA is widely used as a reference benchmark for the uranium sector and is the underlying vehicle that the now-closed Defiance 2x leveraged ETF (URAX) sought to double.
recent: URA posted a year-to-date return of approximately 69% through November 2025, outperforming URNM over that period. It is the primary index vehicle for uranium-sector exposure on US exchanges and continues to trade actively as uranium spot prices rebounded above $100/lb in early 2026 after a volatile 2025 that saw lows near $63/lb.
